authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 5228.1 jihvā gives Prakrit jibbhā, Nepali jib(h)ro and Bhojpuri jībhi, with Maiya zīb. Additional initial y or final -ban requires a source/contamination check; the entry does not establish those changes simply from older links. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open. Comparative check: Mai žīb “tongue” (f_3lx654cstoiyq). The exact survey spelling and phonetic marks remain untouched. Stress, vowel articulation, release marks and source palatal/sibilant notation were reviewed as local details; the full form and sense support the same family. The link does not settle uncertain transfer within Indo-Aryan.
